messages.author: 3cfaef29dbc536f8
messages.subject: Re: LPA using tidyLPA doubt reg
parts:
Murugan, thank you for your message.

Here's what I'd recommend: Save the output from the function to an object, i.e., model_output <- estimate_profiles(d, var1, var2, var3, n_profiles = 3). Then, you should be able to treat model_output as a data frame. Does this work for you? Be in touch.
Josh

parts:
Murugan, I think that you still have all of the data, but perhaps only the first 200 rows are printing.

 

Are you using R Studio? If so, can you run View(model_output)?

 

If you’re not using R Studio, can you run write.csv(model_output, “lpa-model-output.csv”) – and then open that CSV file (i.e., with Google Sheets or Excel)?

 

Josh
